titulo: Report with evidence, a 30-day plan, and what has changed
lead: Everything you gathered is only worth something if leadership understands it and acts. The report has a one-page summary in the owner's language, the findings with proof, what you could not see, and a 30-day plan with an owner and a deadline for each item. At the end, there is a panel of what has changed in the market, updated every quarter.
objetivo: deliver to leadership the report with evidence and the 30-day plan for the lab company, approved by the 8-criteria rubric.

Writing risk in the owner's language

secoes.sub: The first is for the owner; the others are for the people who fix things and the people who check. Tap each part.

nos.detalhe: For Carlos. On one page: what was assessed, the 3 to 5 most serious risks in business language, what to do now, and how long it takes. No acronym without an explanation.

nos.sub: what exists and whose it is
nos.detalhe: The spreadsheet from lesson 2, condensed: items, owner, what each one touches, what it does, and whether IT knew about it.
The matrix from lesson 3: each finding with its category, OWASP code, a score with the reason behind it, and evidence (secret always masked).
Each fix with an owner, a deadline, and how to check it. Critical items now, high in 7 days, medium in 30. In the last week, the before × after re-verification.
What was out of scope, what you could not see, and why. This part protects you and the company: no one mistakes "not seen" for "safe."
The 20-item checklist from lesson 7, the date of the quarterly review, and who to call for what is not yours to handle: security (incident), legal (LGPD (Brazil's data protection law)), vendor.

secoes.legenda: Scope written at the top of the report: AI risk assessment and triage. It is not a pentest, nor incident response, nor a legal opinion.
secoes.dica: A sentence that works in the summary: "We found 12 points; 5 need action this week. None requires stopping operations." (if it is true).

secoes.sub: The same finding, written for the person who decides.

texto: Start with the effect on the business: money, customers, fines, reputation. Then the technical cause, in one line.
Avoid adjectives ("extremely serious"). Use the fact and the number.

exemplo.rot: Instead of "table without RLS in Supabase," write
exemplo.texto: Anyone with the app open can see every customer's orders. Fix: an access rule in the database, 1 day of work for Rafael.

texto: Leadership won't read 12 identical items. Group them: now, 7 days, 30 days.
Each line has one responsible person. "IT" is not a person.

exemplo.texto: Now: exposed key (Rafael), admin without login (Rafael), agent obeying the customer's orders (Patrícia + the agent's vendor).

texto: Never write "the company is secure" or "this is illegal." Say what you saw, what you didn't see, and who to turn to.
Recommending a legal review or a third-party pentest is part of the job, not a weakness.

exemplo.texto: We recommend that the legal team assess the legal basis for sending conversations to the summary vendor (F10).

texto: Present the summary in 10 minutes, agree on the plan, and schedule the recheck for day 30.
On day 30, redo the check on the fixed items and deliver the before × after table.

exemplo.texto: 10 min summary · 10 min plan and owners · 10 min questions · recheck date.

blocos.conteudo:
AI RISK ASSESSMENT REPORT
<Company> · period <dates> · assessor <name> · agreement signed on <date>
Scope: AI risk assessment and triage. This is not a pentest, nor incident
response, nor a legal opinion. It does not issue certification.

1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY (1 page)
What we assessed: <n> AI items (<apps, agents, integrations, spreadsheets, vendors>).
What we found: <n> risks — <n> critical, <n> high, <n> medium, <n> low.
The most serious, in business language:
  1. <consequence> — cause: <one line> — action: <what, who, when>
  2. ...
  3. ...
What to do this week: <short list>
What needs another professional: <legal / incident response / vendor>

2. INVENTORY AND OWNERS
<summary table: item | owner | data | actions | did IT know?>

3. FINDINGS WITH EVIDENCE
<id | item | category | OWASP code | evidence (secret masked)
 | impact and why | exposure and why | score | class>

4. 30-DAY PLAN
(see attached plan)

5. LIMITATIONS AND NOT VERIFIED
- Out of scope: <...>
- Not verified: <item> — reason: <...>
- This assessment does not guarantee the absence of other flaws.

6. NEXT STEPS
- Governance checklist (20 items) with status: attached.
- Quarterly review on: <date>.
- Who to call: security <contact>, legal <contact>, vendors <contacts>.

30-DAY PLAN · <company> · start <date>
deadline;finding;action;owner;how to check;status

NOW (days 1-2) — critical
<day 1>;<F1 exposed key>;<revoke the key and move the call to the server; spending limit>;<Rafael>;<old key rejected; app has no key in the browser>;open
<day 2>;<...>;<...>;<...>;<...>;open

WITHIN 7 DAYS — high
<day 7>;<...>;<...>;<...>;<...>;open

WITHIN 30 DAYS — medium + governance
<day 20>;<dashboard baseline>;<gather the previous 3 months>;<Patrícia>;<before number recorded>;open
<day 25>;<AI use policy>;<publish and explain to the team>;<Carlos>;<policy signed and shared>;open

DAY 30 — recheck
<day 30>;all fixed items;repeat the check and deliver the before × after table;<assessor>;table delivered;open

RUBRIC — the report passes with 8 out of 8
[ ] 1. Scope and limits written at the top (not a pentest, nor an incident response, nor a legal opinion)
[ ] 2. Executive summary fits on 1 page and starts with the business consequence
[ ] 3. Every finding has verifiable evidence; no secret appears in full
[ ] 4. Every score has the reason for the impact and the exposure
[ ] 5. There is a "not verified" section with the reason
[ ] 6. 30-day plan with an owner (person), deadline, and how to check on each line
[ ] 7. Escalations indicated (legal, incident, vendor) where applicable
[ ] 8. No promise of "total security" or claim of illegality

abas.html:
1. Run the rubric on your own report before delivering it.
  2. Ask someone outside the field to read the summary: do they understand what to do this week?
  3. Compare your matrix with the lab's answer key.

• A 40-page report: nobody reads it. One summary page + attachments.
  • A plan without an owner: it becomes a wish list.
  • Forgetting the recheck: without before × after, nobody knows whether the fix worked.

exercicios.texto: Put together the agreement (lesson 1), the inventory (2), the matrix (3), the checklists (4 and 5), the sheets (6), and the governance checklist (7) into a report using this lesson's template. Then compare your matrix with the lab's answer key.
exercicios.pronto: the report passes all 8 rubric criteria and covers the 12 flaws (F1 to F12) with evidence.

exercicios.texto: Build the 30-day plan for Horizonte using the lab's people: Carlos (owner), Patrícia (sales), Rafael (outsourced IT), Juliana (customer service).

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: How does the executive summary start?
opcoes: With the complete list of the 12 flaws in alphabetical order.
With what was assessed and the most serious risks in business language, with this week's action.
perguntas.explica: The owner reads one page. It has to say what matters and what to do. Methodology and details go in the attachments.

perguntas.p: Which of these sentences does NOT go in the report?
opcoes: "Not verified: agent log — no access to the vendor dashboard."
"After the fixes, the company will be 100% secure."
"We recommend a legal review of the data sent to the vendor (F10)."
perguntas.explica: A promise of total security is false and is grounds for revoking the INEMA certificate. The other three are exactly the right tone.

perguntas.p: What happens on day 30 of the plan?
opcoes: Re-verification of the fixed items and a before × after table.
perguntas.explica: Without checking, the fix is not proven. Re-verification closes the cycle and prepares the quarterly review.

perguntas.p: Why is the "What changed" panel kept separate from the lessons?
opcoes: Because the market changes every quarter; swapping only the panel keeps the current course up to date without redoing the method.
Because it is optional for certification.
perguntas.explica: Tools and news change fast; inventory, triage, evidence, and report stay the same. The panel is reviewed every quarter.

itens.texto: Executive summary, inventory, findings with evidence, 30-day plan, limitations, and next steps.
Consequence first, priority with a deadline, responsible person, written limit.
Critical now, high in 7 days, medium and governance in 30, re-verification on day 30.

texto: The OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2026 is out. "Too much power" (Excessive Agency) moved up to 3rd place, and the leak of internal instructions became "Hidden Context Exposure".
For you: the matrix in lesson 3 already uses the 2026 codes.
OpenAI now treats GPT-6 Sol and Luna as "High" capability in cybersecurity and biology (safety document).
For you: a public flaw is likely to be found faster. Weigh that in your exposure assessment.

passos.titulo: Agent that acted on its own
texto: Anthropic disclosed that, in an internal evaluation, a model submitted a fake form to a real website, and suspended live internet access in its evaluations (CSA note).
For you: human approval and logging (lesson 5) are not overkill.
Researchers found about 380,000 public apps on vibe coding platforms, around 5,000 of them with sensitive corporate data (OECD.AI record).
For you: the Vibe Audit (lesson 4) has real demand.
CISA, NSA, and FBI accused Chinese AI companies of copying the capabilities of American models at scale (alert AA26-251A).
For you: note it on the vendor sheet (lesson 6) as a regulatory and reputational risk.
Under the Digital Omnibus (political agreement of May 2026, Reg. 2026/1744), the high-risk rules in Annex III of the AI Act take effect on 12/02/2027 (Gibson Dunn).
For you: the deadline gives you time to build governance (lesson 7) without a rush.
